rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4 report the authors' own one-season lysimeter experiment (nine lysimeters, flood vs surface drip vs subsurface drip, winter wheat) with measured ET, yield components, biomass and gas exchange.
rows.notes: The study does report its own yield data for flood vs drip (Table 1, Section 4.2), but the result does not show a yield increase from drip: flood yield 4694.8 kg/ha was highest, surface drip 4428.0 (5.68% lower) and subsurface drip 4584.8, with all three statistically distinguished (letters a, b, c); the abstract describes SSDI and flood yields as 'similar'. The study's own evidence therefore does not support the claimed yield increase with drip adoption; Q2 answered no because the direction of the finding contradicts the passage. Single soil, single crop, single site, single season; no dispersion statistics given for yield (letter groupings only).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4, own weighing-lysimeter experiment comparing flood, surface drip and subsurface drip on winter wheat at Luancheng station, 2017-2018. Q2: Section 4.1 and Table 2 report that SSDI total seasonal ET (220.96 mm) was about 26% below flood (300.30 mm) and 15% below surface drip, saving about 80 mm of water versus flood, with lower irrigation applied (120 vs 190 mm); Table 3 reports higher irrigation water productivity (17.91 vs 14.40) and crop water productivity (20.75 vs 15.63 kg/ha/mm) under SSDI than flood.
rows.notes: Q3: the water-saving result rests on lysimeter weighing alone; the water balance (Eq. 1) uses the same lysimeter ET, and the one-day leaf gas-exchange measurement (lower leaf transpiration under SSDI, Fig. 6) is a supplementary leaf-level reading rather than an independent determination of seasonal water saving, so no. Q4: the mechanism (reduced soil evaporation because the surface stays dry) is asserted and attributed to cited work [33,41]; soil evaporation and surface soil moisture were not measured separately, and the authors state that partitioning soil and leaf water loss remains to be done. Q5/Q6: one soil, one crop, one site, one season, 0.25 m2 lysimeters; the 4,420 million m3/yr saving for 1.7 Mha of Hebei Plain is an extrapolation. Q7: only generic recommendations (train farmers, adopt SSDI) and a comment that sufficient water must be supplied to protect photosynthesis; no stated requirement for the water-saving effect. Q8: no explicit limitations of the lysimeter result are stated. Q9: Tables 2 and 3 give means with letter groupings only; no SD, SE or CI reported in the text.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-4 report the authors' own lysimeter experiment with measured ET, yield, water balance and leaf gas exchange under flood, surface drip and subsurface drip.
rows.notes: The study contains no observation, measurement or discussion of weeds or weed control under SSDI; it measures evapotranspiration, yield components, biomass, water productivity and photosynthesis only. It provides no own evidence for the weed-control benefit claimed in the passage.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a single-season, single-site, single-soil lysimeter trial with three replicates per treatment; figures are not rendered in the text, so any error bars in Figures 5-6 could not be checked, but tables report means with letter groupings only.
